subject: Muhammad Ali
hook: MUHAMMAD ALI IS NOT WHO YOU THINK
angle: Whether Muhammad Ali threw his 1960 Olympic gold medal into the Ohio River as an act of protest against racial discrimination or lost it accidentally remains a point of contention among his close associates.
angle_support: In his 1975 autobiography, he recalled that shortly after his return from the Rome Olympics, he threw his gold medal into the Ohio River after he and a friend were refused service at a 'whites-only' restaurant and fought with a white gang.

The story was later disputed, and several of his friends, including Bundini Brown and photographer Howard Bingham, denied it. ... Thomas Hauser's biography of Ali stated that Ali was refused service at the diner but that he lost his medal a year after he won it.
title: Did Muhammad Ali Really Throw Away His Olympic Gold?
description: The story of Ali discarding his gold medal in protest is famous, but his own inner circle has long disputed the narrative. We examine the conflicting accounts surrounding the disappearance of his prize.
narration: MUHAMMAD ALI IS NOT WHO YOU THINK You picture him casting his 1960 Olympic gold medal into the Ohio River as a defiant political protest. It was likely a much more mundane, accidental loss. Ali claimed he tossed the medal after being denied service at a whites-only diner. However, associates including Bundini Brown openly mocked that version of events, while biographer Thomas Hauser notes he simply lost the medal later. The truth behind his lost prize remains a contested, lingering mystery.
